official_sources.title: OS OSGM15 accuracy
official_sources.finding: OSGM15 standard error for Great Britain is 0.008 m and excludes GNSS heighting error.

official_sources.title: OSGM15 ellipsoid-to-orthometric model
official_sources.finding: OSGM15 transforms ETRS89 ellipsoidal height to orthometric height; on mainland Britain the target is ODN.

official_sources.title: OSGM15 one-kilometre grid
official_sources.finding: OSGM15 uses the same 1 km grid resolution as OSTN15.

official_sources.title: OSGM15 bilinear interpolation
official_sources.finding: A geoid-ellipsoid separation value at a location is obtained by bilinear interpolation of the OSGM15 grid.

official_sources.title: ODN offshore semantics
official_sources.finding: OSGM15 extends regional datums only 2 km offshore; beyond that an ODN Offshore surface is used and is explicitly lower quality than onshore ODN.

official_sources.title: Regional British height datums
official_sources.finding: OSGM15 incorporates regional datums including Lerwick, Stornoway, Douglas and St Marys in addition to mainland ODN.

official_sources.title: ODN orthometric-height semantics
official_sources.finding: ODN is a mean-sea-level-related orthometric/gravity-related height datum, distinct from GNSS ellipsoidal height.

official_sources.title: ODN benchmark subsidence caveat
official_sources.finding: Legacy benchmark heights can be affected by subsidence, so benchmark agreement cannot silently replace the current OSGM15 route.

official_sources.title: OS preferred heighting route
official_sources.finding: OS identifies GPS plus OSGM15 as the preferred accurate and uniform heighting method rather than unmaintained lower-order benchmarks.

official_sources.title: GNSS versus National Grid height
official_sources.finding: GNSS commonly supplies WGS84/ETRS89 ellipsoidal height while OS mapping uses OSGB36 National Grid and ODN height; a transformation is required.

official_sources.title: National standard OSTN15 OSGM15
official_sources.finding: OSTN15 and OSGM15 are the national standard transformations for GNSS coordinates to OSGB36 National Grid and orthometric heights.

official_sources.title: OS transformation architecture
official_sources.finding: OSTN15 handles horizontal National Grid transformation while OSGM15 handles mean-sea-level-based height transformation.

official_sources.title: Developer raw grid resources
official_sources.finding: OS provides raw OSTN15/OSGM15 developer data with procedures, equations, worked examples and test files.

official_sources.title: Reduced-density lite model warning
official_sources.finding: The Lite developer pack uses a reduced 20 km grid and lower horizontal accuracy, so it must not substitute for the full-resolution terminal model.

official_sources.title: OSGM15 GTX availability
official_sources.finding: OS publishes OSGM15 geoid model data in GTX format for software use.

official_sources.title: Grid InQuest II OSGM15 implementation
official_sources.finding: Grid InQuest II implements OSTN15/OSGM15 transformations offline and is an independent reference implementation channel.

official_sources.title: OSGM15 replaces OSGM02
official_sources.finding: OSTN15/OSGM15 replaced OSTN02/OSGM02 in August 2016.

official_sources.title: OSTN02 to OSTN15 conversion semantics
official_sources.finding: Legacy OSTN02/OSGM02 coordinates require an explicit back-to-ETRS89 then forward-to-OSTN15/OSGM15 conversion path; old and current models are not interchangeable.

official_sources.title: EPSG ODN vertical CRS
official_sources.finding: EPSG:5701 is the valid ODN height vertical CRS for geodesy and engineering survey.

official_sources.title: EPSG compound BNG plus ODN
official_sources.finding: EPSG:7405 is the compound CRS OSGB36 / British National Grid + ODN height.

official_sources.title: EPSG 7405 axis and unit model
official_sources.finding: EPSG:7405 combines easting/northing in metres with gravity-related ODN height in metres and explicitly references EPSG:5701.

official_sources.title: EPSG OSGM15 operation 7711
official_sources.finding: EPSG:7711 is the valid OSGM15 transformation from ETRS89-GBR OSNet v2009 to ODN height, with stated accuracy 0.008 m.

official_sources.title: EPSG OSGM15 model-file identity
official_sources.finding: EPSG:7711 names OSTN15_OSGM15_GB.txt as the geoid height-correction model file.

official_sources.title: EPSG OSGM15 non-reversible operation
official_sources.finding: EPSG:7711 itself is marked non-reversible and points to a distinct reversible alternative, so operation identity and direction must be pinned.

official_sources.title: Superseded OSGM02 operation
official_sources.finding: EPSG:10021 uses OSGM02, has 0.02 m stated accuracy, and is superseded by EPSG:7711.

official_sources.title: EPSG OSTN15 operation 7953
official_sources.finding: EPSG:7953 is the current OSTN15 horizontal transformation and is separate from the OSGM15 vertical transformation.

official_sources.title: OSTN15 1km bilinear grid
official_sources.finding: OSTN15 uses a 1 km shift grid and bilinear interpolation, reinforcing explicit horizontal-versus-vertical grid provenance.

official_sources.title: PROJ OSGM15 GB resource
official_sources.finding: PROJ CDN lists uk_os_OSGM15_GB.tif for Great Britain mainland onshore ETRS89 to ODN height and separately lists OSTN15 horizontal data.

official_sources.title: PROJ OSGM15 resource separation
official_sources.finding: PROJ distributes distinct OSGM15 files for Great Britain, Belfast and Malin, preventing one regional height model from being assumed universal.

official_sources.title: OS coordinate input height semantics
official_sources.finding: ETRS89 geodetic input may include optional ellipsoidal height, whereas National Grid output may include optional ODN height in metres.

official_sources.title: OS mapping datum retention
official_sources.finding: OSGB36 and ODN remain the basis of OS mapping, accessed through ETRS89 using OSTN15 and OSGM15.

official_sources.title: Building-height datum example
official_sources.finding: OS building-height product documentation uses ODN for mainland Britain and regional British datums where applicable, all incorporated within OSGM15.
